game.name: Megabonk
game.short_description: Smash your way through endless waves of enemies and grow absurdly powerful! Grab loot, level up, unlock characters and upgrade to create unique and crazy builds as you fend off hordes of creatures!

commentary.label: Tier list Part 4 (2025)
commentary.summary: Megabonk is a 3D, third-person survivors-like inspired by Vampire Survivors and Risk of Rain 2, where you roam large maps full of shrines and chests. He thinks its hype comes more from its design than from the 3D novelty. He loves the build variety, movement skill and community, but does not place it alongside his S-tier picks such as Blueprints and Night Rain. His verdict is a very solid A tier, possibly limited by his personal taste.
praise: Layered upgrade system: tomes for stat paths, up to four weapons, chest items and shrines with minigames all feed builds
Weapon upgrades roll random attributes with rarities, so a rare or legendary roll that hits the stat you want feels great; the luck stat supports this
Movement is unusual for the genre and has real skill and tech (jumping, sliding for momentum), leading to late-game map-crossing flight
Maps are dense with shrines, chests and interactables, and climbing or falling enemies keep you moving; maps among the best in the genre
Characters scale with every level, and leveling stays frequent into the late game instead of tapering off
Items are mechanically distinct, and every unlocked item can be toggled on or off to avoid diluting the pool
Weekly-reset leaderboards with different metas, a strong community, great music and vibe, and engaging dev logs
criticism: Wants more unique events per run; the bush guy in the first level is a cool surprise but is the same every time
Very hard for a survivors-like; the tier-three bosses and some challenge runs are extremely tough, which he frames as both pro and con
Slightly less crazy late-game enemy hordes ('oozes') than he expected from the hype
Not S tier for him, partly due to personal taste
unique_points: 3D third-person survivors-like, rare in the genre, with movement as a real skill layer
Random attribute plus rarity on each weapon upgrade makes every upgrade feel distinct
Toggling unlocked items on and off solves the item-pool dilution problem common in roguelikes
Constant leveling through the whole run keeps progression rewarding
Community mystery around the anonymous developer and weekly competitive leaderboards boosted its attention
commentary.quote: it's just going to be a very solid A tier.
comparisons: Keeper (the previous game, upgrade system contrast)
design_criteria: Build variety and upgrade system: tomes, weapons, items and shrines give many upgrade routes
Luck and rarity: random rolls with rarities make rewarding moments
Movement and mobility: skill-based 3D movement tech
Level and map design: dense, interactive maps with things to hunt for
Character scaling: per-level gains keep leveling satisfying
Item pool management: toggling unlocked items on or off
Replayability and variety: wants more unique per-run events
Difficulty: very hard for the genre, with tough bosses
Meta and community: leaderboards, dev logs, community engagement
Audio and vibe: music and overall feel praised

commentary.label: Top 10 of 2025 (#5)
commentary.summary: Megabonk is a 3D survivors-like that asks what Risk of Rain 2 would look like as a survivor game. He praises its fast, physics-based movement, varied items, weapons and characters, and interactable-filled levels. The standout is the upgrade system, which combines randomised stat values with player choice and a mechanic for steering stats. He also loves the music, humour and a responsive, secretive developer. It ranks fifth of the year and has become one of his new favourite survivors-likes.
praise: Extensive 3D movement with physics that let skilled players traverse levels fast and precisely
Large pool of items, weapons and characters
Fun level design filled with interactables
Upgrade system: stat and weapon upgrades with randomised values and varying upgradeable stats each time
Tome mechanic lets players prioritise specific stats to curate runs while keeping controlled randomness
Fantastic music, fun vibe and humour
Active community and a developer who keeps updating and listens to feedback
Great balance of automation, strategy and skill in chaotic bullet-and-monster gameplay
criticism: No real criticisms stated in this segment; he only pre-empts the worry that the upgrade system adds too much randomness and says the tome mechanic addresses it
unique_points: Upgrade values and even which weapon stats can be upgraded vary per run, adding a layer of choice
Tome mechanic curates randomness so runs can be steered
Brings Risk of Rain 2 style items and 3D movement into the survivors-like format
design_criteria: Movement: 3D physics allowing high-speed, precise traversal
Content variety: items, weapons and characters
Level design: fun levels filled with interactables
Upgrade/meta systems: randomised upgrades balanced by player control
Community and developer support: constant updates, listens to feedback
Core genre fidelity: chaotic bullet-hell feel with balance of automation, strategy and skill

community.one_liner: A solo-developed 3D survivors-like roguelite that mixes Vampire Survivors-style auto-attacking and build stacking with Risk of Rain 2-style chests, shrines and platforming movement, wrapped in meme-heavy low-poly visuals.
community.consensus_summary: Megabonk launched on Steam on Sept 18, 2025 at roughly $10 and became a breakout indie hit: over a million copies in about two weeks and a peak of roughly 117k concurrent players. Steam currently shows 94.3% positive across about 106.5k reviews (Very Positive). The handful of critic reviews are strongly positive (Metacritic 88 from 4 outlets), praising the addictive loop and movement. Player sentiment has cooled among long-term players: the main complaints are a narrow meta, weak items and balance, grind for unlocks, and a slow update cadence. The game is treated by many as effectively complete or in maintenance mode, and Steam forum threads asking if it is abandoned are common. Even so, the dev did ship patches (1.0.7 through 1.0.12 pinned in the forum) and a Halloween-themed update, and newer reviews show a positive but more mixed tone.
best_things: Extremely addictive 'one more run' loop, the single most repeated praise in Steam reviews
3D movement with jumping, sliding, wall-climbing characters and physics quirks makes it feel distinct from 2D survivors-likes
Good blend of Vampire Survivors auto-combat with Risk of Rain 2-style chest, shrine and item systems
Very low price (about $10 per reviewers; Steam listing showed $5.99 at last check, frequent discounts) for dozens or hundreds of hours; many reviewers have 100-1000+ hours
Wacky busted builds and hilarious late-run physics moments when the screen fills with projectiles
Large unlock and quest list (about 20 characters, 70+ items, 240 quests) and daily leaderboards give goals to chase
Impressive polish for a one-person project; runs fine on Steam Deck and Linux
Humor and memes, dumb-fun presentation and soundtrack land well for many players (a few critics found the music wears thin)
worst_things: Balance: a small set of 'meta' items, tomes, weapons and characters are required to beat the hardest tiers while many others are seen as useless
Luck and XP tomes are close to mandatory, eating passive slots and limiting build variety
Difficulty and enemy HP scaling spike hard at tier 3 / final bosses; runs can feel decided by RNG and meta items within the first minutes
Little enemy variety (mostly walk-at-you damage checks) and only two zones with shared bosses, so runs feel samey
Thin depth for survivors-like veterans: 'mile wide, inch deep', decisions often reduce to stacking damage or projectiles with few real synergies
Some bugs and frustrations noted, such as a boss able to spawn on top of the player, crashes on high-difficulty runs, and a wonky camera/visual clutter late in runs
Humor and meme references are a turn-off for some (IGN called the humor shoddy); community described as toxic by some reviewers
Update cadence: many players feel it reads like an early-access build with a long gap between content updates
improvements: A full balance pass so more weapons, tomes and characters are viable, plus real synergies rather than plain stat bumps
Rework or remove luck/XP tome dependence, for example turning them into permanent shop upgrades, and soften tier 3 enemy HP scaling
More content: additional maps and biomes, distinct bosses per zone, more enemy types
Co-op multiplayer, one of the most requested features (repeated in top positive reviews)
Fix the unlock pool dilution: let players remove or ban unlocked items from the drop pool more effectively
Regular communication and updates from the dev, and less design focus on the optimized YouTuber/leaderboard meta
unique_things: Essentially a 3D Vampire Survivors / Risk of Rain 2 hybrid, where vertical movement, jumping, sliding and fall damage are core
Characters with distinct movement traits (for example a wall-climbing Monke, slow Amog, fast skeleton)
Silver-shop meta-progression gives only rigging tools (rerolls, bans, skips) and no permanent stat upgrades, so each run starts equal
Chest cost scales with each chest opened, Risk of Rain-style, alongside shrines that offer percentile boosts
Daily leaderboards with Steam friends and a physics engine that lets builds get absurd; meme-heavy 90s low-poly art style
Built by a solo dev (Vedinad, widely speculated to be DaniDev of Crab Game and Muck) which became part of its story
tedious_or_disliked: Grinding for unlocks and quests; some achievements need things like a 300k-kill run or beating the hardest boss with a slow character while RNG cooperates
Resetting runs repeatedly to hunt for meta items, which players call an 'RNG reset simulator' at higher tiers
Item pool dilution: each new unlock makes desired items drop less often
Late-game visual clutter and boss mechanics (for example orb pushback during pillar charging in the desert final boss)
Early-game levels feel slow at base movement speed, with some saying faster movement requires exploiting an engine quirk
Shallow modifiers (gold, silver, knockback) that feel meaningless
Having to fill 2 of 4 passive slots with XP/luck/difficulty boosters every run, which reviewers call lame and build-limiting
divisive_points: Whether the game is 'finished': defenders say a $10 game with no microtransactions owes nothing more, critics say it feels like early access and is abandoned
Meme humor and aesthetic: charming and funny to many, cringe to others
Difficulty and meta: some see hard tier 3 as an enjoyable challenge and a skill issue, others see it as forcing the same builds
Whether it is a derivative combination of Vampire Survivors and Risk of Rain 2, or a fresh and well-tuned blend of them
community.reception_notes: Launch was a viral success (1M+ copies in about two weeks, about 117k peak CCU, early Steam reviews around 95%+ positive). It was delayed two weeks from Sept 4 to Sept 18, 2025 to dodge Hollow Knight: Silksong. The dev withdrew the game from The Game Awards 2025 Best Debut Indie nomination because of prior work under other names, and the game was later nominated for a Steam Awards category. Critics (Destructoid, PC Gamer, Gamereactor, TheGamer, Rogueliker) were very positive; IGN was more mixed, citing limited map variety and humor. Post-launch, long-term players turned critical over balance and update gaps, with a first major (Halloween) update arriving around December and several patches later (1.0.12 pinned), plus community forum threads asking whether the game is abandoned. A newer Steam review (about a year after release) defends the dev for finishing a cheap game. Windows and Linux only per Steam (no Mac). Note: 'Megabonk Apocalypse' on Steam is an unrelated title by another publisher (TinyBig). Sales are the Wikipedia figure; SteamSpy and revenue-calculator data pulled locally were empty. OpenCritic page could not be located (search budget exhausted, guessed IDs returned other games).
